Hi Priya — thanks for the clear questions and for the RFP snippet. High level response below and I can convert this into a one-pager / option matrix for legal/procurement. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if that helps.

Summary (short):
- Keystore economics: two model choices. 1) HSM seat (annual seat fee) — predictable, good for high-throughput signing/attestation. 2) Usage credits (per-KMS-op) — lower upfront but variable cost as you scale.
- Onboarding fee: we can apply up to 40% of the onboarding implementation fee as a one-time credit against the first-year HSM seat cost, or amortize as monthly credits against usage for the first 6 months.
- Evidence deliveries: treated as a recurring evidence subscription when cadence > quarterly; one-time when it is a single delivery. We propose a monthly evidence subscription for Crestline (weekly extracts per RFP) — we can offset the first 3 months with onboarding credits.

I attached a sketch (RDW_keystore_pricing_sketch.pdf) with the two options and a simple worked example for your expected auditlog volume. Do you want me to draft the option matrix for legal or would you prefer a short call with procurement and security together?

Best,
Ben Carter
Sr. GTM — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Ben / Karthik — thanks for the clear breakdown. I support offering the two options (seat credit or amortized usage credits) with the following guardrails: 

1) Cap the total onboarding credit applied to any single customer at $35k to protect margin on small deals. Crestline's ask is within range.
2) Evidence subscription credit: limit to first 3 months and require milestone accepting the weekly extracts (i.e., evidence success sign-off) before applying month 2/3 credits.
3) Require procurement to sign a 12-month minimum commitment for the HSM seat if they choose the annual seat option; if they churn before 12 months we claw back unused credit pro-rata on final invoice.

If Karthik concurs I'll approve the credit and Ben can send the option matrix to Priya with the updated guardrails and a DocuSign link for the SOW.

Marissa Cole
